newsitem.title: USA: CBMM raises ferro-columbium production capacity.
newsitem.headline: CBMM raises ferro-columbium production capacity.

text.p: Brazil's Companhia Brasileira de Metalurgica e Mineracao or CBMM is raising its ferro-columbium production capacity to 30,000 tonnes by year end to keep its dominant position, the company's U.S. sales subsidiary, Reference Metals Co said.
Harry Stuart, Reference Metal's executive vice president, said CBMM's current capacity is 25,000 tonnes per year of the micro alloy used in steelmaking, known outside the U.S. as ferro-niobium.
CBMM's output this year will be 15,000 to 17,000 tonnes of ferro-columbium, with world consumption at 22,000 to 23,000 tonnes, Stuart said.

"CBMM has always had a policy that they alone could satisfy world demand if necessary," Stuart said. "Growth has been significant in the last few years and it's enough to warrant that we think about our policy."
Other, much smaller producers of ferro-columbium include Brazil's Mineracao Catalao de Goias, and Niobec in Canada, a joint venture between Teck and Cambior.

Earlier this year, Reference Metals said CBMM probably had enough columbium reserves to last a thousand years, and prices was likely to remain stable for the forseeable future after barely changing in the past 20 years.
